findings.reason: the write-path list is the node's binding scope, so a builder implementing as written would leave the dispatch refused by a reader the plan never named, and the fix is to carry the project on the pace row (reckon/pace_report.py `pace_row`, which today records `session` for precisely this reason) and read it in that guard, plus a case standing up a project lift and showing the guard admits the dispatch it cleared.
findings.text: the deliverable says a project lift "covers every dispatch whose project matches" and names the readers the project must reach (`_config_with_effective_budget` in routing.py, `effective_block` in budget_group.py, `_effective_budget_block` in snapshot.py), but leaves out `_refuse_against_the_bookend_reserve` (reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:292), called from the dispatch path at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1800, which resolves its own block with `effective_block(..., session=pace_record.get("session"))` and no project — so under a project lift that guard keeps the bookend reserve and can refuse a project-A dispatch that `_budget_verdict` admitted, exactly the dispatch the lift was granted to let through

findings.reason: `reckon/crew/resumption.py` is not among the write paths, so the deliverable's claim that a project lift covers every dispatch of its project would be false for a resume, and the plan should either name that file and add a parity case or state that a resume is out of the lift's scope.
findings.text: the same omission appears on the resume path: `_readonly_budget_verdict` (reckon/crew/resumption.py:964) resolves the group block as `effective_block(config, group, readings=None, now=None, session=None)`, so with no project it cannot see a project lift, and its one caller `_launcher_refusal` (:1012) is consulted at :1948 ahead of both the dry-run and the real resume branch, so a project-A run is skipped as held by a real resume sweep while a fresh dispatch of the same project is admitted by the launcher's own chain (routing.py -> budget_group.py -> budget_lift.py) — the prediction-versus-launcher disagreement §49 closed for the credit lift
